what: Every World Bank or IFC project ICIJ found with confirmed or possible displacement, 2004-2013, as a lead list for new cases. Read likely_already_on_map and r17_outcome before researching any row. ROUND 17 FINDING, which governs how every figure in this file should be read: ICIJ's displaced figure is NOT a count of people relocated. It is ICIJ's count of project-affected people, and on ICIJ's own account of its method it searched Bank documents for 'affected', 'PAP' or 'displaced', used average household size where only households were counted, and because the documents did not distinguish temporary from permanent impacts it 'decided to include all impacts'. In several rows it is the appraisal plan figure rather than the outcome. Verified examples: Liaoning Medium Cities, where ICIJ's 31,547 is to the person the people figure in the ORIGINAL resettlement plan while the outcome was 2,467 households and 6,080 people; Distribution Efficiency, where ICIJ gives 31,581 and the completion report says only five households were relocated out of 12,880 project-affected households; Second Rural Energy, where ICIJ gives 773,838 and the appraisal gives 178 families losing more than 10% of productive land. ICIJ's ** marker means, on its method page, a project affecting more than 20,000 people where Bank documents said most impacts would be minor. Use the Bank document's own outcome figure for a case and put ICIJ's in a note, named, with what it counts.

source.title: Evicted and Abandoned: the World Bank's broken promise to the poor
source.note: Harvested from ICIJ's own per-country tables, one page per country, 124 countries. Every figure here is ICIJ's, copied as printed: project name, approval date, status, cost and estimated people physically or economically displaced. ICIJ's data is as of 31 December 2014. 968 projects, of which 422 are in its confirmed-displacement table, which is ICIJ's own published count.

fields.section: which of ICIJ's three tables the project sits in
fields.displaced: ICIJ's estimate, blank where it prints none or Unknown
fields.complaint: ICIJ lists it under Projects with complaints
fields.iso3: every country page the project appears on
fields.likely_already_on_map: keyword match against case titles, places and ids in the same country; weak means two shared words, strong three or more. A hint, not a finding: confirm before dropping a row.
fields.matching: likely_already_on_map and possible_overlap are keyword hints, not findings. They match rare words shared with a case in the same country, so two projects in the same state can match each other. Confirm a row before dropping it; nothing has been deleted from these lists.
